title_candidates: Test ChatGPT Images 2.5 with one controlled edit
ChatGPT Images 2.5 makes follow-up edits easier to check
summary: ChatGPT Images 2.5 promises faster generation and more controlled follow-up edits. A fictional poster test lets you check what changes and what stays put.

primary_source.title: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.5
primary_source.author: OpenAI
key_facts: ChatGPT Images 2.5 improves detail, lighting, texture, reference-photo fidelity, and instruction-following during edits.
OpenAI says image generation latency is up to 50 percent lower than with Images 2.0.
The model is designed to change requested elements while preserving subjects, composition, and surrounding details.
Across successive edits, earlier changes are more likely to remain intact without image quality declining over time.
ChatGPT adds Sketch for drawing visual guides, templates for common formats, image comments for targeted edits, and optional prompt sharing.
Images 2.5 is rolling out across all tiers of ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex on desktop, mobile, and web.
OpenAI says supported generated images include C2PA metadata and invisible watermarking alongside prompt and image safety checks.

quote_candidates.text: Sharper details, faster generation, more precise editing, and better tools for creating and sharing.
Images 2.5 is better at editing only what you’ve asked for, while keeping the rest of the details the same

supporting_sources.title: Images in ChatGPT
key_facts: OpenAI's help center says ChatGPT Images is available on all tiers on web, iOS, and Android.
Users can create an image from the Images area, edit a selected region or describe a change conversationally, and save the result.
The editor's selection highlight may be imprecise, and an edit can extend beyond the selected region.
Images are automatically kept in the Images library until the associated conversation is deleted.

supporting_sources.title: Provenance signals in OpenAI-generated content
key_facts: Supported images generated with ChatGPT, Codex, and the OpenAI API include C2PA metadata and SynthID watermarks.
OpenAI Verify can check a supported file for those provenance signals.
A detected signal does not prove an image is accurate, unedited, legally owned, or shown in the correct context; a missing signal also does not prove an image was not AI-generated.

prerequisites: A signed-in ChatGPT account on web, iOS, or Android
No sensitive personal photo; the test uses a fictional poster

steps.instruction: Open ChatGPT, choose Images from the sidebar or More menu, and submit: Create a square travel-poster illustration for the fictional Moonlight Botanical Fair, with a glass greenhouse, navy sky, warm lanterns, and the exact title MOONLIGHT BOTANICAL FAIR. Confirm a square image appears and check whether the title is readable.

Open the generated image, choose Select, highlight one lantern, and request: Change only this lantern to bright turquoise; keep the title, greenhouse, layout, and every other color unchanged. Compare the result with the original and note every requested and unrequested change.

Add a second edit in the same conversation: Add three small fireflies above the greenhouse and change nothing else. Confirm that three fireflies appear, then check whether the turquoise lantern, title, greenhouse, and layout survived the second turn.

Select the finished image and choose Save. Confirm the file downloads and that the image remains available in ChatGPT's Images library; keep the original and final images side by side for your comparison.

Upload the saved fictional poster to OpenAI Verify and inspect the result for an OpenAI provenance signal. Treat a match only as an origin clue, not proof that the picture is accurate or unedited, and remember that a missing signal does not prove human authorship.

risk_flags: Images 2.5 is rolling out, so the newest controls may not appear on every account immediately.
The editor selection can be imprecise and edits can extend outside the highlighted region, so the guide requires a side-by-side check.
Provenance signals are origin clues, not proof of accuracy, ownership, editing history, or context.
Sketch is mobile-specific and templates are not available in Work mode, so the guide does not depend on either feature.
